findings.one_line: The proposal's sharp full-class indegree-two frontier (matching upper and lower bounds) is still explicitly unresolved; the delivered effective Dubé cutoff is a materially weaker object and must be repositioned as such rather than presented as fulfillment of that frontier promise.

The theorem needs a precise comparison to the cited birational inverse-degree literature (especially Hassanzadeh--Simis) explaining why its graph-ideal cutoff is not implied by, or comparable to, those inverse-degree bounds; the current related-work text gives that citation no relevance sentence.

For a fixed deterministic pole-free rational map, this is a standard finite-dimensional delta-method/Wald corollary; either state a theorem-level distinction from the cited fixed-estimator inference literature or demote it to a clearly labeled usability corollary rather than count it as a novel main contribution.
